newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close lower, but volume buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close lower, but volume buoyant.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower on profit-taking by local investors, but turnover was supported by foreign buying of blue chips, brokers said.
The all share index closed 2.1 points down at 615.4. Sampath Bank fell 1.25 rupees to 45, and Vanik 50 cents to 17 rupees.
"You may see the index coming down a few more points because there still is a little more profit that can be taken," said Deva Ellepola, a trader at Jardine Fleming.
Retail investors who took the all share index up from around 608 points in late October, are taking profit and waiting to see where the index would settle before returning, he said.
Brokers say the next resistance level could be around 610 points.
Turnover was 47.8 million rupees on 789,475 shares. Foreign buying and selling was even at 38 million rupees each.
The main trades of the day were foreign buying of 53,600 Development Finance shares and 102,000 John Keells Holdings shares.
"Foreign investors collect these blue chips whenever they become available in volume," said Rohan Fernando, a trader at brokerage CT Smith.
